bull_bear.body: All capex via internal accruals; no fresh debt. Conservative "sustainable & secure business" posture — 100% advance required for new Africa merchant-export customers in first 6 months. No M&A named for bi-metal/Alkop (organic).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Monsoon/drought → tractor-segment softness (mgmt: "not worry," scrappage + govt capex offset).
- Geopolitics: Strait of Hormuz/West Asia war stalled merchant-export orders for ~3 months last quarter (now restarted); Rs 65-75 cr guidance is "subject to good monsoon and geopolitics not worsening."
- Dynamometer slippage risk on railway timeline.
- Raw-material timing gaps; consumable inflation not passed through.
- Brakes 25% margin flagged as mix-driven, may normalize.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular, promoter-led; transparent that brakes' 25% is product-mix (not to be annualized) and that Rs 360 cr is deliberately conservative. Track record of beating own guidance (Rs 270 cr target → delivered Rs 300 cr). Refused to give hard railway numbers pre-dynamometer ("don't want to give concrete numbers"). Grounded on defence ("very stringent … 2-3 years") and robotics ("different field, not exploring").
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Alkop revenue can't be reverse-engineered from tonnage — Rs 900+/kg realization is raw-material-inflated, not volume; value-add is the real driver.
- The margin beat is *understated* quality: achieved while absorbing 300% carbide-tool inflation and with peak (Q3/Q4) seasonality still ahead.
- The Rs 500 cr target moving from FY30 to "2-3 years" is the biggest positive delta vs prior quarters.
- Infrastructure (buildings/land) already sunk for the next Rs 500 cr — incremental capex is only machinery at 2.5x asset-turn, so growth is high-ROCE.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Bi-metal (Bearings):** utilization ~80-87%; peak revenue capacity >Rs 400 cr on current machinery; single-source to John Deere >20 yrs; adding Rs 9-10 cr capex for +25-30% capacity. EBITDA margin 21%+.
- **Alkop (Aluminium die-casting):** realization risen to Rs 900+/kg (raw-material-driven; base ~Rs 700 at Rs 200-250 aluminium, now Rs 340-370); utilization 65-70%; EV customers TACO Prestolite, Tata Motors (Curvv/Punch EV), Eaton Concentric; moving to 1,600-ton HPDC parts. EBITDA ~21%.
- **Brakes:** 25% EBITDA this quarter (vs 12-14% historically) on product mix + halted low-margin Dubai/Africa exports; utilization 65-70%; entered 2W, entering 3W; railway + OEM optionality post-dynamometer.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Integrated, high-value-add niche:** deliberately avoids commodity passenger-car bearings; focuses on heavy-duty tractor/engineering/industrial critical parts where value-add is higher and overheads minimal. Zero-PPM (parts-per-million rejection) certifications from multiple OEMs; OEE "up to global standards" → cost of production structurally lower, enabling reasonable pricing + margin.
- **30-40 yr sticky OEM relationships** (John Deere single-source >20 yrs; customers "older than me"); reliability/after-sales drives the next RFQ. Supported Allison through tariff period at margin cost — converted into more US RFQs. Third-generation promoter continuity.

latest_quarter.body: Blended EBITDA ~21.5-22% (bi-metal > Alkop > brakes as the structural order, though brakes led at 25% this qtr on mix). Cu/Al up 20-25% and freight/consumables (carbide +300%) up sharply — Cu/Al passed through via indexing, consumables absorbed. Mgmt guides sustaining 20-21% blended; brakes to normalize toward 20% as low-margin exports resume.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Highest-ever Q1 on all lines — consol revenue Rs 91.79 cr (+36.6%), PAT +67% (EPS Rs 2.52). Brakes EBITDA 25% (mix-driven). US/Canada roadshow → Rs 65-75 cr incremental pipeline (FY27-28); domestic RFQ Rs 75 cr @ 75-80% strike. **Rs 500 cr target pulled forward from FY30 to 2-3 years.** FY27 Rs 360 cr held (conservative). Dynamometer now Aug-Sep 2026. Capex Rs 9-10 cr bi-metal + Rs 4 cr Alkop, internal accruals.
- _Next Q → check: dynamometer actually commissioned (Aug-Sep) + first railway order; US engine-bearing supply starting Q3-Q4; Alkop Rs 100 cr FY27 trajectory; export mix moving toward 37%; brakes margin normalizing from 25%; Europe (Sept) visit conversions; H2 seasonal step-up vs Rs 360 cr._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 guidance Rs 360 cr held (explicitly called "a conservative figure … we will stick to that"); could exceed on export momentum. Q4 "much better scenario" flagged.
- **3-year:** 20%+ YoY growth (conservative; "can be 25%"); **Rs 500 cr target pulled forward** from FY30 to "next 2-3 years."
- **Alkop (aluminium):** Rs 100 cr FY27 → Rs 125 cr FY28 (vs ~Rs 80 cr annualised run-rate).
- **Export mix:** rising to ~37% of revenue next year (from 24-30% historically).
- **Alkop EV share:** 8-10% by FY27-end (currently 4-5%).
- **Railway (brakes):** dynamometer commissioned by **Aug-end 2026**, technical rig running by Sep-end; RDSO/vendor-code registered; Rs 5-6 cr business year-1 → Rs 25-30 cr within 2 years.
- **New-order pipeline:** Rs 65-75 cr incremental from US/Canada (FY27-28) + Rs 75 cr domestic RFQ list at 75-80% strike → >Rs 60 cr additional this/next year. Africa direct: bearings/bushes/washers ~Rs 9 cr + brake linings Rs 6-7 cr/yr.
- **Capex:** Rs 9-10 cr bi-metal (FY27, +25-30% capacity, ~Rs 25 cr revenue potential) + Rs 4 cr Alkop; future capex asset-turn ~2.5x; all internal accruals.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **US/Canada (June roadshow):** RFQs/NDAs from Magna (9 aluminium plants in Canada, buys ~Rs 1,800 cr/yr), Allison Transmission, Linamar; incremental Rs 65-75 cr over FY27-28. US-based person hired to compress the 9-12 month realization to 6-7 months. Engine-bearing/bi-metal RFQs already converting (supply expected Q3-Q4 FY27); Alkop samples by CY2027.
- **Domestic:** Rs 75 cr RFQ list at various stages (feasibility→sample→PPAP→approval), 75-80% strike rate.
- **Europe:** Sept 2026 15-day visit (CNH/New Holland invited them to European suppliers; Netherlands offered business) — realization FY27-28.
- 37 parts already approved; 51 new parts under development.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: China+1 / rupee-depreciation export capture (US, Canada, Europe, direct Africa); EV die-casting (Alkop 4-5%→8-10%); railway braking (Vande Bharat, metros, cargo/passenger bogies — dies already built); aerospace (Honeywell wheel parts, airport lighting — exploratory); secondary defence exposure via Allison washers (US). Not pursuing humanoid robotics or primary defence.

deepdive.thesis: Record quarter on every line — highest-ever Q1 sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT — with consolidated revenue +36.6% YoY to Rs 91.79 cr and PAT +67% (EPS Rs 2.52 vs Rs 1.50), achieved *despite* war-driven consumable inflation (carbide tools +300%) that they fully absorbed. The growth story is now explicitly export/China+1-led: a June US/Canada roadshow (Magna, Allison, Linamar) generated RFQs/NDAs worth an incremental Rs 65-75 cr over FY27-28, on top of a Rs 75 cr domestic RFQ pipeline (75-80% strike). Brakes surprised with 25% EBITDA (vs 12-14% historically) on product mix; the delayed railway dynamometer finally commissions by Aug-Sep 2026.
